prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Select Your Desktop Companion Path", "Choose Companion Path"]
1: ["Sign in to securely bind your pet creation to your account profile."]
2: ["Check your uploaded photos and chosen companion attributes before final adoption.", "Confirm & Generate", "Verify Pet Photo & Style Details"]
3: ["Learn how to trigger commands, access settings from the tray icon, and summon your pet.", "Right-click system tray icon to access pet settings or put your pet to sleep.", "Got It", "Mastering Desktop Pet Controls"]
4: ["Signing in connects your pet to cloud saves so progress and pets are never lost on reset."]
5: ["Initializing desktop graphics overlay... Your pet will pop onto your screen shortly."]
6: ["Use the system tray icon to hide, feed, or adjust pet settings anytime. Press Alt+P to center pet.", "Your Pet is Live on Your Desktop!"]
7: ["Certified Desktop Companion"]
8: ["Chime on Complete"]
9: ["Select a quick preset companion or build a custom pet using your own photos.", "Pick Your Companion Style"]
